name: AAA Club Alliance (Partner)
desc:
Remote Emergency Roadside Telephone Responder | $16 to $19/hr | Inbound Roadside Assistance Calls, No Sales Expectations
Company: AAA Club Alliance
Industry: Customer Service

What Your Day Will Look Like:
You'll answer 40 to 60 calls a day from AAA Members whose cars have broken down. You'll find out where they are using online maps, enter their vehicle and what they need, and set up the tow and where it's going. You'll listen for safety concerns or hardships so the most urgent calls get priority, then tell members what to expect, like the estimated arrival time and any cost. When it fits the call, you'll mention AAA programs or discounts that could help. Calls get busy during bad weather, so weekends, overtime, and holidays may be needed.

Soft Skills
- Staying calm under pressure
- Empathy for stressed callers
- Active listening
- Quick, sound decisions
- Accurate typing while talking
assessment: AAA recently updated their hiring assessment. Every applicant now completes a pre-hire assessment that includes basic computer skills, web browser knowledge, technology terminology questions (including things like HDMI and iOS browser navigation), and a typing test. Minimum recommendation is 25 WPM. Applicants below 25 WPM typically receive additional training before being considered. The assessment measures existing knowledge, not something you can prepare for with notes.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma or equivalent
Required Experience: 1 year of customer service experience
Preferred Experience: Call center or inbound call experience, Salesforce, and map reading

Required Skills:
- Clear written and verbal communication
- Multitasking and staying professional during high call volume
- Good computer and typing skills
- Attention to detail
- A quiet, private workspace with no distractions
- Hard-wired ethernet internet (no Wi-Fi, DSL, hotspot, satellite, or shared connection)
- Must live in an eligible state, and Oklahoma is eligible
- Can't be caring for others in the household while working

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Has a year of customer service and stays calm when callers are stressed
- Wants an early morning schedule with full-time or part-time options
- Is comfortable using maps and online tools

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Is caring for kids or family members at home during work hours
- Doesn't have hard-wired ethernet internet
- Can't work one weekend day a week or extra hours in bad weather
- Gets overwhelmed taking 40 to 60 calls a day
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening went, expect an email to schedule an interview
This is an estimated process. Paid virtual training starts November 30, 2026.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Inbound call center
- Roadside assistance
- Emergency dispatch
- High call volume
- Customer service
- Online mapping tools
- Data entry accuracy
- Call prioritization
- Salesforce
- Empathy and de-escalation

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about your customer service or call center experience.
- A caller is stranded on the highway at night and panicking. How do you handle the call?
- How would you find someone's location if they don't know exactly where they are?
- Tell us about a time you stayed calm during a very busy day. What happened, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you had to make a quick decision for a customer. What was the situation, what did you decide, and how did it turn out?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: $16 to $19/hr (confirmed for Oklahoma), plus an 8% shift differential for regular shifts after 1:00 p.m. Central.
-Shift: Full-time options start at 6, 7, 8, or 9 a.m. Central (8-hour shifts). Part-time options start at the same times (6-hour shifts). Everyone works one weekend day a week, and weekends, overtime, and holidays may be needed in bad weather.
-Benefits: Full-time gets medical, dental, vision, and prescription, a 401(k) with up to 7% match, 2+ weeks of PTO in the first year, paid holidays, up to 2 weeks paid parental leave, free AAA Membership, and up to $5,250 a year in learning reimbursement.
-Equipment Provided: Yes, all required computer equipment is provided. You need your own hard-wired ethernet internet.
-Felony Friendly?: Case by case
-Drug Test: OMMA friendly
-Notes: Oklahoma is an eligible state, and AAA Club Alliance is a WRO partner. Paid virtual training starts November 30, 2026, and runs 3 weeks, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Central. Camera must be on for all training and meetings. You can't care for anyone in the household while working. Participants pick a full-time or part-time schedule before training ends.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Roadside Telephone Responder → Senior Responder or Dispatcher → Roadside Assistance Contact Center Supervisor I → Contact Center Manager. AAA has posted a Roadside Supervisor I role that doesn't require supervisor experience, so there's a real ladder. This role builds call center, dispatch, and decision-making skills.
training: Starts 11/30/2026, 3 wks paid, M-F 8AM-3:30PM Central, camera on
